earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog lists no descriptive work for Chaungtha (only an ISO change request and Bradley 1995 intro); treated as a Burmese dialect.

sources.citation: Okell, John. 1995. Three Burmese dialects. In David Bradley (ed.), Papers in Southeast Asian Linguistics No.13: Studies in Burmese languages, 1-138. Pacific Linguistics A-83. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: online with a Harvard login (also: harvard online access (harvardkey))
sources.note: Arakanese (Sittwe) chapter: p.3 identifies Chaung-tha as the minor northern variety of Arakanese; p.7 sec.2.2.1.1 tone inventory heavy/creaky/low/stop/'weak', 'Phonemes are as for SB except as set out below'; sec.2.3.2.2 pp.16-17 'Weakening' (AR reduces first syllables to schwa more than Standard Burmese). The word 'stress' is never used; no accent-placement statement.

sources.citation: Bradley, David. 1985. Arakanese vowels. In G. Thurgood, J. A. Matisoff & D. Bradley (eds.), Linguistics of the Sino-Tibetan area: the state of the art, 180-200. Pacific Linguistics C-87. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: Harvard print copy (Scan & Deliver or loan); the journal or volume is held, not the item itself: WID Offsite Storage PL3521.L56 1985
sources.note: p.189: schwa vowel carries no tonal contrast and marks a 'reduced syllable'; words have 'one reduced syllable in a two-syllable word; and the first or second, or even the first two in a three-syllable word' (i.e. final syllable always full); sec.5 Tones pp.197-198: four tones realised as in Burmese. No use of 'stress'.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page chau1262 (Hammarström et al.), https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/chau1262
sources.note: Bookkeeping entry, merged into rki per CR 2011-043; no descriptive references.
Mentions 'Chaungtha (upper river)' as an area of dialect variation; phonology section (from Okell 1995, Houghton 1897) says nothing on stress, tone or reduced syllables.

sources.citation: Davis, Heidi A. 2014. Consonant correspondences of Burmese, Rakhine and Marma with initial implications for historical relationships. MA thesis, University of North Dakota.
sources.note: p.8 lists Chaungtha among Rakhine dialects in Myanmar (after Ethnologue 17); thesis treats consonants only, tone omitted; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2011. Change Request Number 2011-043: adopted merge [ccq], adopted merge [ybd], adopted update [rki] (effective 2012-02-03). Dallas: SIL International. 5 pp.
sources.note: Nothing; p.2 merges Chaungtha and Yangbye into Rakhine [rki]; p.4 cites an unpublished 2011 Myanmar sociolinguistic survey (wordlists from Kyauktaw Township and Yangbye Island) plus Bradley 1985, Okell 1995, Matisoff 1986.

sources.citation: SIL International / LSDO Myanmar. 2011 (unpublished). Sociolinguistic survey of Rakhine varieties (wordlists, interviews from Kyauktaw Township [Chaungtha area] and Yangbye Island), cited in ISO 639-3 CR 2011-043 as 'publication delayed due to local sensitivities'.
